status: complete_first_pass: merged from press_expedition.json, oneil_expeditions.json and other_history.json; every text copied byte-for-byte from those drafts.
what_this_is: The game's pool of verbatim lines from public-domain sources: the 1889-90 Press Expedition (1890 newspapers and The Mountaineer of 1907), Lt. Joseph P. O'Neil's 1890 report (Senate Doc. 59, 1896) and his men's 1907 accounts, The Mountaineer of 1907-1920, S. C. Gilman (National Geographic, 1896), the USGS survey (1902), Meany's place names (1923) and Proclamation 869 (1909). It feeds the epitaph dice (GAME_DESIGN 9.5), narrator asides, camp readings and summit pages.
rules: No line by Robert L. Wood is in this file, or ever may be: his books are in copyright (see wood_bibliography.json). Lines licensed from his rights holders, if any, would go in lore/wood_licensed_lines.json.

Every line is printed exactly as fetched: 1890 spellings (to-day, indorsement), misprints ('depts'), [sic] spellings ('hurculean', 'Quinaiult') and lower-case starts are kept. Curly quotes were made straight; words split by end-of-line hyphens were joined. Two drop capitals were set in normal case (see 'normalization').
public_domain_reason on each line says why: published in the United States before 1931, and/or a U.S. government work (17 U.S.C. 105).
Only lines with verification 'page_image_checked' may be dealt by the dice. Lines seen only in a modern transcription are in held_back and are never dealt.
A dealt line never mentions a death, an injury or a named person (GAME_DESIGN 9.5). The 'not_an_epitaph_because' field records why each short line was refused.
Frame 'unknown land' and 'first to see' lines as 1890 attitudes, never as fact: the peninsula's tribes knew these mountains long before (see history.json indigenous).

fields.id: Stable id: pe_ = press_expedition.json, on_ = oneil_expeditions.json, oh_ = other_history.json, then the draft's id. The Trail Register stores this id with a dealt line.
fields.text: Verbatim, exactly as printed in the source.
fields.chars: Length as printed (Python len of the string).
fields.fits_epitaph_40: True if the line fits the 40-character epitaph field as printed.
fields.epitaph_ok: True if the line works as an epitaph (60 characters or fewer, stands alone, kind, names nobody, no death or injury). Includes the 41-60 character lines that would need a wider field.
fields.drawable: True if the dice may deal it today: epitaph_ok, fits_epitaph_40 and page_image_checked. Same as 'epitaph' in suggested_uses.
fields.voice: explorer (a member's own words), expedition_report (the Press report as condensed in 1907), newspaper (1890 summaries and editorials), later_writer, reference (Meany, Collier's), official (the proclamation). The dice deal explorers first.
fields.credit: The small credit printed under a dealt line.
fields.cause_tags: Which causes of death the line suits: river, tide, cold, fall, dark, crevasse, lightning, fog, hunger, snow.
fields.caution_causes: If present, the dice may deal this line only for these cause keys.
fields.suggested_uses: epitaph (dealable now), epitaph_long (41-60 chars, needs a wider field), narrator_aside, camp_reading, night_page, trip_start, trip_end, summit_page, hazard_warning, near_miss_page, history_note, store_page.
fields.node_ids: Park nodes the line belongs to (validated against regions/*.json).
fields.origin: The draft file and id the line came from.

epitaph_dice.rule: GAME_DESIGN 9.5: each death shuffles its own deck. Lines tagged for the cause come first (preferred), then the general pool; within each, explorers' own words come before newspaper summaries (the lists below are already in that order; shuffle within a voice band). A line with caution_causes is dealt only for those causes. The deck never repeats until it runs out.
epitaph_dice.note_on_dark: 'dark' is the *You have died of the dark.* variant of a fall or cliff death; it uses the fall deck with dark-tagged lines first.
epitaph_dice.note_on_hunger_snow: hunger and snow are tags, not cause keys: snow lines feed cold, fall and crevasse; hunger lines sit in the general pool (no hunger death exists in the game).
